Prince Harry has condemned Russia’s intensified missile and drone attacks on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, calling them “a sign of desperation.” He made the remarks following a visit to Lviv, urging the international community to step up its support for Ukraine and do more to end the war. “The increase in Russian missile and drone strikes on civilian infrastructure is simply a sign of desperation. [...] I find it appalling that civilian infrastructure, especially hospitals and medical centers, is being targeted. Humanitarian aid centers are also being targeted,” he said. Prince Harry also expressed disappointment with the West’s response to Russia’s repeated attacks, warning that Ukraine’s resilience should not become an excuse to scale back assistance. “International law must mean something. [...] The fact that Ukraine has managed to adapt to life amidst the war is a truly remarkable achievement. However, witnessing their resilience should not lead us to weaken our support. On the contrary, we must redouble our efforts to put an end to this. We cannot simply sit back and wait for things to resolve themselves. We are capable of doing more to bring this war to a close,” he emphasized.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei warned that new US allegations about Iran developing chemical or biological weapons echo the claims used to justify the 2003 invasion of Iraq. In a post on X, Baghaei recalled former US Secretary of State Colin Powell's presentation at the UN Security Council, accusing Washington of weaponizing unsubstantiated intelligence to build public support for the invasion. He also asked whether the world had learned from the consequences of the Iraq War or would once again allow similar allegations to pave the way for military action.

🇺🇸 🇻🇪 🇬🇾 ⚡️ — A Trump administration official suggested that Guyana consider ceding part of its territory to Venezuela, alarming Guyanese officials and prompting Washington to reaffirm its recognition of Guyana's borders, according to Reuters, citing three people familiar with the matter. State Department policy chief Jeremy Lewin offered to facilitate negotiations over the resource-rich Essequibo region, which Venezuela has long claimed despite being internationally recognized as part of Guyana. Lew maintained that the discussions were authorized by the White House, while the State Department insisted that U.S. policy regarding the disputed territory had not changed.

Тоді його має виконати Національна поліція. За це має проголосувати комісія», — пояснив депутат. Заява прозвучала напередодні засідання ТСК 23 листопада, на яке запросили директора НАБУ Семена Кривоноса, керівника САП Олександра Клименка, ексголову СБУ Василя Малюка та інших посадовців. 🇺🇦 Реальна Війна | Підписатись
